html: A migraine is more than a bad headache. Attacks often bring pounding pain, nausea and a need to get away from bright light and noise, and they can last from a few hours to a couple of days. Some people notice warning signs, like flashing lights or zigzag lines, before the pain starts.

• Stress, or a sudden letdown after a stressful stretch
  • Too little or irregular sleep
  • Skipping meals
  • Hormone shifts, such as around a period
  • Some foods and drinks, including alcohol

• Track attacks in a diary or app to spot patterns
  • Lie down in a dark, quiet room when an attack starts
  • Ask your care team about medicines that stop attacks and, if they're frequent, prevent them
A sudden, explosive headache; a headache with fever and a stiff neck, confusion, weakness or trouble speaking; or a headache after a head injury.

title: Migraine
abstract: What a migraine attack can involve, common triggers and when a headache is an emergency.
